title: "Components, workflows & modularity"

## The building blocks

OpenPipelines is assembled from components built using  [Viash](viash.qmd), a tool that turns a plain script into a runnable, containerized unit.

We use these terms to refer to different parts of OpenPipelines:

```{=html}
<div class="concept-list">

  <div class="concept-card">
    <div class="ct">Component</div>
    <p>
      The computational unit that performs a single task.
      A component consists of a <code>config.vsh.yaml</code> that defines inputs, outputs and other arguments, as well as the computational environment, along with a script that is run (Python, R, or Bash).
      Viash builds a containerized, self-contained tool from these files.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="concept-card">
    <div class="ct">Workflow</div>
    <p>
      A workflow is a component where the script is a Nextflow <code>main.nf</code> file that runs other components in order, passing data between them.
      Every component can become a step in a workflow, and every workflow can be composed as a subworkflow within a larger workflow, to create complex pipelines.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="concept-card">
    <div class="ct">Module</div>
    <p>
      We call the runnable Nextflow form of a component or workflow a module.
      These are generated by Viash from the component files and include additional functionality beyond a standard Nextflow workflow.
      A module is built from every component so an individual process can be run using Nextflow in the same way as a workflow.
    </p>
  </div>

</div>
```

## Code-level vs. execution-level modularity

OpenPipelines is modular at both the code and execution levels.

### Code-level modularity

Code is organized by component or workflow.
Components can be considered similar to functions in a package and used or swapped as needed.
Shared code such as environment definitions or helper functions ensure consistency between components and reduce maintenance.

### Execution-level modularity

OpenPipelines components are also modular at the execution level.
Every module is an independent containerized unit that can be run on its own or chained together to form workflows.

- **Self-contained**: Each component has its own Docker image with the packages it requires.
  Two components can have conflicting dependencies but still run in the same workflow.
- **Independently runnable**: Each component can be executed, tested or built without needing the rest of the project.
  Built components can be run as executables or Nextflow modules.
- **Consistent data format**: Components in OpenPipelines store data in the [MuData](mudata.qmd) format.
  Using a consistent data format means components can easily be rearranged or substituted without needing additional data manipulation.

## Why modularity is important

The modular design of OpenPipelines means that constructing a workflow becomes a matter of combining the correct steps.
Adding, removing or swapping a processing step is a change to the pipeline definition but does not need modifying individual components.
Components can be reused in multiple workflows and shared across the OpenPipelines [ecosystem](ecosystem.qmd).
